answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The tide multiplier is published, charged in basalt, and atlas lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1995 identities would post 1285 proofs and burn roughly 74 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
